verdict.note: `failed` counts real functional failures only; mutant runs are reported separately via the verdict block.
harnessDefectsFoundAndFixed: Every mutant at HEAD was 'caught' as an IMPORT FAILURE: the harness rewrote ./positions and ./hover to absolute paths but not ./relations, so the mutated copy could not load. A load error was counted as a behavioral catch (§8.7: the tautological gate). Fixed by deriving the rewrite from the source's own relative imports and by recording an import failure as a FAILURE of the harness.

Two mutant anchors matched zero or two occurrences and the harness printed 'SKIP (anchor not found)' and continued — so a rename would silently delete a mutation without changing the verdict. Fixed: a missing or ambiguous anchor is now a FAILURE.
The oracle returned a bare boolean, so a catch could not say WHICH law broke. Now it returns {caught, detail}, and the log names the law.
verdict.lintJudgedNote: Two mutants are invisible to any oracle on results — the hand-rolled byte walk is behaviorally almost right — and are judged by the source-level §5 rule 1 lint instead. That lint is its own script (script/m24/verify-position-arithmetic.ts) so it cannot be edited away with this suite.

determinism.note: Re-running this verifier at an unchanged commit reproduces every field byte-for-byte EXCEPT the three named above. generatedAt is a wall-clock stamp; bbSeal.sealedAt is the write time; bbSeal.contentSha256 is a sha256 over the record's content, which includes generatedAt, so it changes with it. All three are declared here as volatile (contract §8.2 allows regeneration modulo declared timestamps). No other field is time-, path-, or order-dependent: the fixture is temp-dir based and every emitted collection is sorted or in insertion order.
determinism.measured: Two consecutive runs of `npx tsx script/m24/verify-navigation.ts` compared after canonicalising the three declared volatile fields: identical. The same comparison holds for validation/m24/results/POSITION-OWNERSHIP.json across two runs of its own verifier.

the declared-absence reason reaches the wire only through src/lsp/server.ts, which is not this lane's file — see `wiringNeededInServerTs` below. This gate proves the component carries the reason; it cannot prove the editor receives it.

the launch gate keys off the file EXTENSION (languageForPath), not brain_file.language. A file whose extension maps to a launch language while its rows say otherwise is served; a file the extension cannot classify is declared absent with language:null.
§15.3 omission count is per-response (omittedUnresolvable); the reasons behind each omission are in the per-row absence from edgeLocationDetailed, which the references result does not enumerate.
wiringNeededInServerTs: src/lsp/server.ts:573 (textDocument/definition) — `if (!r.found || r.location === null) return null` discards r.absence. The LSP wire shape for definition is `Location | Location[] | null`, so the reason cannot ride the result; it needs either a window/logMessage carrying the reason, or an accepted deviation recorded here.

src/lsp/server.ts:607 (textDocument/references) — `return r.locations.map(navLocationToWire)` turns a declared absence into a bare `[]`, which contract §11.7 calls a violation ('silent empty results that look like no references found'). LSP 3.18 requires Location[] for this request, so the honest options are: (a) a window/logMessage with r.absence.detail, or (b) the client reading a custom field — neither is available on this wire shape.

src/lsp/server.ts:547 (textDocument/hover) — `if (r.contents === null || r.range === null || r.data === null) return null` discards provenance.limitations, which already names the language and the launch set. Same wire constraint as above.
